name: WooCommerce
description: WooCommerce orders become events on each buyer's profile: Placed Order once it's paid, Fulfilled Order, Cancelled Order and Refunded Order (once per refund, its own amount), with the order's items and currency. Customers become profiles held back from marketing, because WooCommerce has no marketing opt-in field. Past orders import through the REST API.

signature_secret.label: WooCommerce webhook secret
signature_secret.help: The Secret you type when you add each webhook (WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → Webhooks). Use the same secret for all of this integration's webhooks.

credentials.name: consumer_key
credentials.label: REST API consumer key
credentials.help: Used to read each refund's record and to import past orders. WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API → Add key, with Read permission. Starts with ck_.

credentials.name: consumer_secret
credentials.label: REST API consumer secret
credentials.help: Shown once next to the consumer key. Starts with cs_.

setup: Create the integration from this recipe and copy its webhook URL.
Pick a long random secret and save it as the integration's signing secret.

In WordPress, go to WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → Webhooks → Add webhook. Name it DumbMail orders, set Status to Active, Topic to Order created, Delivery URL to the webhook URL, and Secret to the same secret. Save.
Add three more webhooks the same way, with the topics Order updated, Customer created and Customer updated.
Place a test order (or open a webhook's Logs) and check the delivery log. A paid order shows up as Placed Order on the buyer's profile.

In the Pull tab, change your-store.example.com to your store's address, and save a REST API key with Read permission as the credentials consumer_key and consumer_secret. DumbMail reads each refund's own record with it (its date, and whether the payment gateway refunded the money), and imports past orders when you Import history from a start date. Imported orders are marked historical; their refunds aren't imported.

Buyers are held back from marketing (WooCommerce doesn't record a marketing opt-in). Only tick "Everyone this integration adds has agreed to get marketing email from us" if that is true for every customer.
